target_customer: Employers needing temporary, seasonal and temp-to-hire hourly blue collar workers (warehouse, events, drivers)
problem: Traditional temp agencies are slow and inefficient at screening, matching and dispatching blue collar workers.
business_model: Staffing agency margin on W-2 hourly workers supplied through an app and platform

founders.name: Gino Rooney
founders.background_notes: Built In (2019-06-11) calls him co-founder and CTO while the YC page lists him as CEO; roles conflict.

founders.name: Cooper Newby
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page. Built In says two Stanford graduate students founded BlueCrew in 2014 without naming them, so Stanford is not attributed to anyone.

exit.reason: IAC sold its Bluecrew business to Apollo-backed EmployBridge for cash and combined-company stock; terms undisclosed. Announced 2022-10-04, completed 2022-11-09.

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace and dispatch software with screening and time tracking; the hard part was operations and W-2 compliance, not research level technology.

defensibility.rationale: Local worker pools and client relationships helped, but gig staffing apps and traditional agencies could replicate the model.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not copy it directly in sources found. IAC owned Bluecrew by 2022 and sold it to EmployBridge, a large industrial staffer.

market_need_then: Built In (2019) names traditional staffing agencies and Craigslist as the alternatives. EmployBridge cited a roughly $40 billion light industrial staffing market in 2022.

branding.domain_note: Used bluecrewjobs.com rather than an exact .com

identity.voice_and_tone: Flexibility and quality: workforce flexes to meet needs, pre-screened W-2 workers

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press and Built In coverage; Great Place to Work certification mentioned on its site. No evidence of community or brand driven growth, and the name is easily mistaken for other crews.

outcome_analysis: Bluecrew grew from a Stanford founded startup into a W-2 staffing platform in 25+ markets with about 100 people on the YC listing and $17.3M raised by the end of 2018 per Built In. IAC owned it by 2022, then sold it to EmployBridge in a cash and stock deal that closed November 2022 at an undisclosed price, so profitability and investor returns are unknown.
notes: Rounds not recorded: Built In says $17.3M raised by end of 2018 with no investors named; aggregators give conflicting figures ($720K seed May 2015, $14M 2018 IAC corporate investment, $47.6M total on one site with implausible 2013 dates, $120K on CB Insights). None verified. How and when IAC acquired Bluecrew was not found. EmployBridge release and Bloomberg pages were identified from search results and not opened. No dated competitor source near 2015 found (Instawork and Wonolo pages are recent competitor marketing), so list is empty. Rooney role conflict noted above.
